mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on (a) Team A's shots FOR vs Team B's shots AGAINST, and (b) Team B's shots FOR vs Team A's shots AGAINST, treating both asymmetric pairs together. Team A produces ~13.3 shots/game and Team B concedes ~14.5 shots/game (both well above the competition mean of ~12.4), while Team B produces only ~9.0 shots/game and Team A concedes only ~9.6 shots/game. The mechanism asks: when one side has a large shot-production surplus AND the opponent has a large shot-concession surplus, while the other side has a shot-production deficit AND the opponent has a shot-concession deficit, does the aggregate shot total and the within-match shot asymmetry between the two teams diverge from what either single-team mirror would predict?
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Aggregate shots in the fixture rise above competition baseline, and the within-match shot split is asymmetric (Team A producing disproportionately more shots than Team B), with the asymmetry larger than either team's own FOR/AGAINST mirror alone would suggest.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume advantage over Team B is structurally large (Team A FOR shots vs Team B FOR shots), but Team B concedes shots at a much higher rate than Team A concedes shots. The joint relationship between each team's shot production and the opponent's shot-concession rate — considered simultaneously rather than as two separate mirrors — determines whether the aggregate shot environment in this fixture is elevated, suppressed, or asymmetric relative to competition norms.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is not a single-observable mirror. It requires jointly conditioning on two distinct asymmetric observable pairs (Team A shots FOR × Team B shots AGAINST, and Team B shots FOR × Team A shots AGAINST) simultaneously, which cannot be reduced to one observable with one band. The structural asymmetry between the two sides — one team dominant in shot production, the other suppressed — is the joint signal.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on the direction and magnitude of the recent-vs-long-run shift for BOTH teams simultaneously: Team B shots FOR (RECENT_5 ~13.8 vs ALL_PRIOR ~9.0, a large upward shift) combined with Team A shots AGAINST (RECENT_5 ~12.6 vs ALL_PRIOR ~9.6, also an upward shift). The mechanism tests whether the co-occurrence of both teams showing the same directional recent shift in the same observable produces a compounding effect on the fixture-level total beyond what either shift alone predicts.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams simultaneously show an upward recent-form shift in the same observable (shots), the fixture-level total for that observable rises above what either team's individual recent-vs-long-run adjustment would predict additively.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shots FOR in recent matches (RECENT_5: ~13.8) has surged dramatically relative to its season-long average (~9.0), while Team A's shots AGAINST in recent matches (~12.6) has also risen relative to its season average (~9.6). The joint recent-form trajectory of both teams' shot-related observables — not just one team's recent vs long-run — may signal a regime shift in the fixture's shot environment that neither team's individual recent-vs-long-run comparison captures alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: A single team's recent vs long-run is already covered. This mechanism requires the joint conditioning on both teams' recent-vs-long-run shifts in the same observable at the same time — a two-team, two-window interaction that is not reducible to one observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team A corners FOR by half (1H vs 2H) and Team B corners AGAINST by half (1H vs 2H), and (b) Team B corners FOR by half (1H vs 2H) and Team A corners AGAINST by half (1H vs 2H). This is a within-match state (half-level) conditioning applied simultaneously to both teams' production and concession profiles — four half-level series interacting, not a single observable with one band.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The second half produces a higher share of total match corners than the first half, driven by the joint second-half elevation in both Team B's corner concession rate and Team A's corner concession rate, with the half-level imbalance larger than either team's individual half-split would suggest in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner-kick production is heavily skewed toward the first half (FOR 1H: ~3.0 vs FOR 2H: ~2.99, near-equal split) while Team B concedes corners heavily in the second half (AGAINST 2H: ~3.25 vs AGAINST 1H: ~3.13). Simultaneously, Team B produces very few corners in the first half (FOR 1H: ~1.97) but more in the second half (FOR 2H: ~2.22), while Team A concedes more corners in the second half (AGAINST 2H: ~2.32 vs AGAINST 1H: ~1.97). The joint half-level asymmetry across both teams' corner production and concession profiles — conditioning on both the half dimension and the team-role dimension simultaneously — determines whether the corner distribution within the match is front-loaded, back-loaded, or asymmetric between the two teams across halves.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on the half-level split (within-match state) for two distinct team-role pairs (Team A FOR vs Team B AGAINST, and Team B FOR vs Team A AGAINST). It is not a single observable with one band; it is a joint four-series half-level interaction.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team A goals FOR by half and Team B goals AGAINST by half, and (b) Team B goals FOR by half and Team A goals AGAINST by half. The mechanism tests whether the joint half-level interaction of both teams' scoring and conceding profiles produces a within-match goal-timing distribution (more goals in one half vs the other) that differs from what either team's individual half-split predicts.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The first half produces a disproportionate share of Team A's goal threat (relative to Team B's goal threat), while the second half is where Team B's goal threat is concentrated; the joint half-level asymmetry means the two halves have structurally different goal-scoring dynamics between the two teams, with the first half more one-sided and the second half more balanced.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goal production is strongly skewed toward the first half (FOR 1H: ~0.85 vs FOR 2H: ~0.975, with 1H representing a higher share relative to competition norms), while Team B concedes heavily in both halves but especially in the first half (AGAINST 1H: ~0.82, AGAINST 2H: ~1.04). Simultaneously, Team B scores almost exclusively in the second half (FOR 1H: ~0.34 vs FOR 2H: ~0.64), while Team A concedes more in the second half (AGAINST 1H: ~0.41 vs AGAINST 2H: ~0.56). The joint half-level goal-scoring and concession profiles of both teams interact to create a within-match goal-timing structure that is asymmetric: Team A's threat is relatively more front-loaded while Team B's threat is back-loaded, and this joint asymmetry cannot be captured by either team's half-split alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on the half-level split (within-match state) for two distinct asymmetric team-role pairs simultaneously. It is not a single observable with one band; it is a joint four-series half-level interaction across two teams' scoring and conceding profiles.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) both teams' recent-form foul rates (RECENT_5) being simultaneously elevated above their respective season averages and above competition baseline, and (b) the asymmetry between Team B's yellow-card FOR rate and Team A's yellow-card FOR rate. The mechanism asks whether the co-occurrence of elevated joint foul rates AND a structural yellow-card asymmetry between the two teams produces a compounding effect on second-half card totals.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half cards (cards_2h) rise above competition baseline when both teams simultaneously show elevated recent foul rates, with the effect amplified by the structural yellow-card asymmetry between the two teams; the joint signal is stronger than either team's foul rate or card rate considered in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's recent fouls FOR (~13.4, RECENT_5) and fouls AGAINST (~14.6, RECENT_5) have both surged well above their season averages (~10.3 and ~10.8 respectively) and above the competition mean (~11.9). Team B's recent fouls FOR (~12.8) have also risen above their season average (~10.3). The joint condition of both teams showing elevated recent foul rates — combined with Team B's structurally higher yellow-card rate (FOR ~1.66 vs Team A's ~1.42) and Team A's higher cards-2h AGAINST rate (~1.23 vs competition ~1.31) — creates a compound disciplinary pressure signal. The mechanism tests whether the joint elevation of fouls across both teams in recent form, combined with the asymmetry in yellow-card propensity between the two teams, predicts an elevated second-half card environment beyond what either team's foul or card rate alone would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This mechanism involves three distinct observables (fouls, yellow_cards, cards_2h) jointly, conditions on both teams' recent-form shifts simultaneously, and incorporates a within-match period (second half) for the outcome variable. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one band; it requires the joint interaction of two teams' foul trajectories and their card-rate asymmetry.
